perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He is Harold Padilla, a project manager, and he has been feeling frustrated and anxious because his project team seems unmotivated and project progress is suffering.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer friend/advisor whom he relies on for advice in stressful work situations.
- At the coffee shop, Harold told Arthur his team seemed completely unmotivated and it was affecting progress. Arthur advised him to understand what drives each team member individually and to have one-on-one conversations so they feel valued and understood. Harold agreed to try this and felt more hopeful.
- Harold told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful; Team Member 2 said they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each of them.
- After implementing Arthur’s advice, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried and told Arthur this. Arthur suggested there might be deeper issues—personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors—and that Harold might need to dig deeper. Harold decided to set up another round of meetings.
- In those one-on-one meetings, Harold asked team members to share concerns. Team Member 1 told him there was tension between a few team members that was affecting work. Team Member 2 told him they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, which made motivation hard. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, and told them their well-being mattered.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered. He told the team they would have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help; Team Member 2 agreed it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad and that their input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.
